title: Writing from the start, and the violinist uncle
summary: He began composing as soon as he returned to music, writing violin and piano pieces for his uncle, whose professional acceptance meant more than family praise.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Were you at that point doing composition and beginning to learn to write and thinking of writing?
I was doing it from the very beginning, and I think when I went back to
music after those few years away from it, probably the first thing I did was start to write.
For the kids bands and such or performance things for you, for piano?

I had an uncle that was a violinist, I would write violin and piano things because he would visit very often and we'd play together, or whatever was available to me, in terms of other musicians and what they played. I'd write for them.
How did your uncle feel about your work then? Presumably he was something of a traditionalist.
He was a pretty good egg. Excuse me. Where were we?
Your uncle's response to what you were writing. He was obviously used to playing printed music from Schirmer or something.

The things I wrote he handled very well. What I meant to imply, he wasn't like my mother or my aunt who used to tell me I was the greatest thing that ever lived, which I couldn't take, it turned my stomach. My uncle was cool. He didn't praise me, but I could tell by the way he worked with me that what I was doing was acceptable to him on a professional level. That was all I needed. That was enough reassurance, which was genuine.
The compliments that I got from the rest of my family weren't genuine.
